h1: The 6 Best Freestanding Room Dividers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six freestanding room dividers compared on width, weight, hinges, feet and wheels for studios, offices and shared bedrooms.
summary: The SUNALLY 4-panel is the best freestanding room divider: 88 inches wide with widened feet and the only lockable wheels here, in the $50 to $100 bucket. The Legacy Decor is the best solid wood shoji screen, and the MAYOLIAH covers the widest span at 120 inches. The RANTILA is the lightest at 8.8 lbs.
intro: A freestanding divider has exactly one job, which is to stay upright when nobody is holding it. Most that fail do so at the base. Narrow feet, a thin frame and heavy panels turn a screen into a lever, and one brush from a passing elbow sends it over. Fabric choice and color come a distant second to how the foot is built.

We reviewed eight dividers on paper and ranked the six that cover the main uses, comparing listed width, height, weight, feet and hinge design from the spec sheets. Prices appear as buckets because they shift often. The top picks all lead with a foot or mobility feature, because stability decides whether a divider is useful or a nuisance.

products.name: SUNALLY 4-Panel Room Divider with Lockable Wheels
products.verdict: An 88 inch screen with lockable wheels and widened feet.
products.description:
The SUNALLY is a four-panel divider, 88 inches wide and 72 inches tall, built from 240g polyester over a powder-coated steel frame. What sets it apart is mobility: it is the only divider in this ranking with lockable wheels, plus extended, widened feet. Wheels let one person slide a full-size screen across a floor, and the locks hold it still once it is placed. It sells in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It takes first place because it combines stability and flexibility in one frame. The HOMSCREENER matches it on width and fabric weight but has no wheels, so it stays fixed. The Legacy Decor beats it for looks but cannot be rolled.

Buy it for a shared room or home office whose layout changes. The caveat is the extra hardware, so engage the wheel locks whenever it is in place. Skip it if the divider never moves.
products.skipIf: The divider stays in one place.

products.name: Legacy Decor 6-Panel Shoji Room Divider
products.verdict: A solid wood shoji screen, 105 inches wide at 22 lbs.
products.description:
The Legacy Decor is a six-panel shoji screen, 105 inches wide and 71 inches tall, with a solid wood frame, translucent panels and two-way hinges. It needs no assembly and weighs 22 lbs, the lightest six-panel wood screen in this set. Translucent panels pass light while hiding detail, which suits a living room where the screen is part of the decor. It sells in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It takes second because wood and shoji panels give real furniture appeal, though that look costs it the SUNALLY's wheels and lower price. Against the MAYOLIAH, it spans less, 105 inches to 120, but it looks like a piece of furniture instead of a barrier.

Buy it for a living room where appearance matters. The caveat is cost: it sits in the pricier 00 to $200 tier, and with no wheels, moving a six-panel wood screen takes two hands.

products.name: MAYOLIAH 6-Panel Folding Privacy Screen
products.verdict: A 120 inch span that reconfigures from 2 to 6 panels.
products.description:
The MAYOLIAH is the widest screen here at 120 inches by 72 inches across six panels. It uses 180g polyester on an iron frame with a powder-coated finish, and it has wider support feet, a one-year warranty and five configuration options from two to six panels. Reconfiguring matters because a long straight screen is the least stable shape, while a zigzag stands on its own geometry. It sells in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It lands third because its 180g fabric is lighter than the 240g polyester on the SUNALLY and HOMSCREENER, and it lacks wheels. In return, it covers more floor than any other pick and reshapes to fit.

Buy it for large or open-plan rooms. The caveat is that 120 inches needs real floor space to stand, so skip it in a small studio.

products.name: HOMSCREENER 4-Panel Fabric Room Divider
products.verdict: An 88 inch fabric screen on 17.7 inch feet.
products.description:
The HOMSCREENER is a four-panel fabric divider, 88 inches wide and 71.3 inches tall, with 240g polyester on a steel frame. Its feet are 17.7 inches wide, the most clearly stated foot width in the ranking, and the triple-buckle hinges hold the folds in place. The fabric is wrinkle-resistant. It sells in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks fourth because it matches the SUNALLY on width and fabric but has no wheels, so it is less flexible in a changing room. The wide feet are a real stability benefit, though, and a fixed screen needs nothing more. Against the MAYOLIAH, it trades span for a heavier fabric.

Buy it for a bedroom or studio corner where the divider stays put. The caveat is the fixed position: without wheels, moving it means lifting. Skip it if you rearrange the room often.
products.idealFor: A fixed bedroom or studio corner.

products.name: RHF 6 ft. 4-Panel Rattan Room Divider
products.verdict: A rattan-style boho divider for under $50.
products.description:
The RHF is a four-panel boho divider, 63 inches wide and 72 inches tall, with a rattan-style frame, woven fabric panels, two-way hinges and a five-medallion diamond weave. It needs no assembly and costs under $50. Two-way hinges mean the panels fold in either direction, which makes zigzag setups easy.

Fifth place follows from its span. At 63 inches, it covers far less than the 88 inch fabric screens, and its rattan-style frame is not solid wood like the Legacy Decor. It is the cheapest decorative divider in the set, and for a bedroom corner or a plant stand backdrop it is enough.

Buy it for a boho bedroom or a corner that needs hiding. The caveat is the narrower span, so skip it if you need wide coverage. Check the feet when it arrives, since a lightweight frame depends on the base staying flat.

products.name: RANTILA Single Large Panel Room Divider
products.verdict: A single 71 inch panel at just 8.8 lbs.
products.description:
The RANTILA is a single large panel, 71 inches wide and 69.5 inches tall, with an HDPE and steel frame, UV-protected waterproof fabric and four stiffeners for stability. It weighs 8.8 lbs, the lightest here. Waterproof, UV-protected fabric means the panel can stand on a patio without fading or soaking through. It sells in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Sixth place follows because a single panel does not fold, so it is less versatile than the multi-panel screens. You cannot zigzag it for stability or reconfigure the span the way you can with the MAYOLIAH. Its low weight and weather resistance are what set it apart.

Buy it if you move a divider often or want one outdoors. The caveat is that it does not fold flat like a hinged screen. Skip it for a living room where the screen needs to stand alone and look like furniture.
products.skipIf: You want a folding hinged screen.

whatMatters.detail: Feet are the base that keeps a screen upright, and wider or extended feet resist tipping far better than narrow ones. Most tip-overs start at the base, not the panels. Look for foot width in inches, such as the HOMSCREENER's 17.7 inches, or wording like widened or wider support feet in the bullets.

More panels cover more width but need more floor space, and a long straight run is the least stable shape. Divide your needed span by the listed width. A four-panel 88 inch screen suits most rooms, while the MAYOLIAH's 120 inches suits open-plan spaces. Measure your opening before ordering, and leave a few inches for the feet.

A lighter screen is easy to move but can feel flimsy, while a heavier wood screen stays put once placed. The RANTILA lists 8.8 lbs and the Legacy Decor 22 lbs. Compare stated weights and decide whether you move the divider or park it. A listing that states weight at all is usually more trustworthy than one that hides it.

Wood, steel, iron and rattan-style frames differ in look and durability. Steel and iron resist bending, solid wood looks like furniture, and rattan-style frames suit a light, decorative role. Check the materials line, and note whether the frame is powder-coated, as on the SUNALLY and MAYOLIAH. Steel and iron suit a screen that gets moved often.

Lockable wheels let you reposition a divider without lifting it and then hold it steady, while two-way hinges let panels fold in either direction for zigzag layouts. The SUNALLY is the only one with wheels here. Look for these terms in the bullets, and confirm the wheels lock, because rolling wheels with no brake let a screen drift.

faq.q: Will a freestanding divider tip over?
faq.a: Wide feet help a lot, because a screen tips when its base is narrower than its height suggests. The HOMSCREENER lists 17.7 inch feet and the SUNALLY has widened feet. Keep any screen on a flat floor, avoid leaning on it, and fold a long run into a zigzag for extra stability.

faq.q: Do any of these have wheels?
faq.a: Only the SUNALLY, with lockable wheels. The Legacy Decor, MAYOLIAH, HOMSCREENER, RHF and RANTILA are fixed on feet, so moving them means lifting. If you rearrange often or clean under it weekly, the wheels are the deciding feature.

faq.q: Is the Legacy Decor worth it over a fabric screen?
faq.a: If you want solid wood and a shoji look, yes. The Legacy Decor costs more but works as furniture. Fabric screens like the SUNALLY or HOMSCREENER are cheaper, lighter to move and fold more flexibly, but look less like furniture.

Not for the Legacy Decor or RHF, which both list no assembly required. The fabric screens fold out on hinges and need little setup. Unfold, space the panels evenly, and check the feet sit flat before leaving it.

Yes. The MAYOLIAH reconfigures from two to six panels with five layout options, which lets you fit a narrower space. Fold the extra panels back and use a zigzag for stability, since a straight run is the weakest shape.

faq.q: Can I use the RANTILA outdoors?
faq.a: It lists UV-protected, waterproof fabric on an HDPE and steel frame, so it suits patios better than the fabric screens. Check the manufacturer page for limits, and secure or weight the base against wind, since a flat panel catches gusts like a sail.

finalTake: Pick the SUNALLY for a room you rearrange, the Legacy Decor when the screen is a design feature, and the MAYOLIAH for open-plan spans. The HOMSCREENER suits a fixed corner, the RHF a boho budget, and the RANTILA movers and patios. Judge the feet before the fabric, because a divider that tips is worth nothing.
